structural_observation: Three rounds, three wrong statements of one rule (§b1 -> §b2a bullet 1 -> §b2a:102), each asserted by a _demo built from the example that produced the wording. The demo confirms the sentence rather than testing it, so the loop is re-deriving prose from whatever shape was last in hand instead of from the mechanism in normalize.py.

findings.claim: R8's acceptance is not met: the third statement of the §b2a rule is still false in general — an image with its cell's visible text on BOTH sides lands inside that cell, which falsifies both 'only when that span's own visible text begins exactly at the mark' and 'the only shape that is'; the rule is contradicted by §b2a's own row 3 and by the _demo assertion that pins it, is copied into the output contract, and the identical falsified sentence from round 2 survives verbatim in the shipped case's provenance.
findings.evidence:
specs/decisions/ADR-032-image-reference-annotation.md:102 ('an image lands inside a span **only when that span's own visible text begins exactly at the mark and continues past it**') and :109 ('**inside** the cell (offset == cell start). The only shape that is'), mirrored into the output contract at specs/001-sec10k-contract.md:141. Counterexample, a signature-block cell a filer really writes: `/s/Darren W. Woods` -> image offset 12, cell (9, 27), so 9 <= 12 < 27 is INSIDE its own cell while the cell's text begins at 9, not at the mark. The ADR also contradicts itself two lines later: :111 says the `
text
` image is 'still inside the **table**', and src/sec10k/normalize.py:551 asserts exactly that — e.jpg at offset 23 inside table (15, 31) whose visible text begins at 15, not at 23. Neither the mid-cell shape nor the general rule is pinned by any assertion; _demo enumerates five positions, none of which is `texttext`. Separately, evals/adversarial/images-in-table-cell.json's provenance still carries, unchanged by this diff, 'So an image in a cell that carries text does land inside that cell' — the exact sentence R8 falsified and that the author's own pr44-r2-resolution.json calls 'false for TWO of three' shapes.

findings.acceptance: §b2a states the condition that is actually true — containment is just `span.start <= offset < span.end`, i.e. the span has visible text at or before the mark and visible text at or after it — with 'begins exactly at the mark' demoted to the sub-case it really is, and row 109 loses 'The only shape that is' (or gains the mid-cell shape); specs/001-sec10k-contract.md:141 carries the same corrected wording; the falsified 'an image in a cell that carries text does land inside that cell' sentence is removed from evals/adversarial/images-in-table-cell.json's provenance; and `normalize.py::_demo` pins the `texttext` mid-cell shape (inside its own cell) so a fourth wrong restatement goes red. Row 110's bare '**outside**' also names WHICH span, since in _demo's own instance c.jpg at 19 is outside its cell but inside table (15, 31).

findings.claim: The new corpus sentence '**The corpus is entirely the fourth case**' is false for 4 of the 10 in-table corpus images it counts — cvx-2015's four sit in a wholly text-empty `<table>` that is never recorded as a table at all, a sixth outcome the 'all five shapes' enumeration omits.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-032-image-reference-annotation.md:115 (changed in this diff from 'second case' to 'fourth case') claims all 10 are row 4, `` in an image-only LEADING row 'outside the whole table: every empty cell is clamped forward to the tightened table start while the image stays behind it'. Measured on the corpus: ba-2003 50321, bac-2006 391006 x2 and xom-2021 232186 x3 do have a table record starting 2 chars later (leading-row clamp, 6 of 10); cvx-2015's wtibrent.jpg 133962, natgas.jpg 137973, consoldinc10feb.jpg 145599 and cashdebt27jan.jpg 166482 have NO table record anywhere near them (nearest records (127392,128503) and (145616,145697)) because their enclosing `...` contains no visible text and is dropped entirely — there is no tightened span for the image to be outside of. specs/001-sec10k-contract.md:145 ('ADR-032 §b2a enumerates all five positions') inherits the same gap, and evals/adversarial/images-in-table-cell.json's provenance carries the older 'The corpus is entirely the second case' with the same cvx-2015 4-of-4 count.

findings.acceptance: §b2a splits the corpus count honestly (6 of 10 leading-row clamp: ba-2003 1, bac-2006 2, xom-2021 3; 4 of 10 cvx-2015 in a text-empty table that is not recorded, so there is no span at all), the shape enumeration adds that sixth outcome (or stops claiming 'all five'), specs/001:145 matches, and `normalize.py::_demo` pins a wholly text-empty table producing zero table records with the image offset still emitted — so a future 'entirely case N' claim about cvx-2015 goes red.
